assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Endoplasmic reticulum
items.clue: A network of membrane tubules and flattened sacs continuous with the outer membrane of the nucleus.

items.label: Genus
items.clue: A group of closely related species that share similar traits, named by the first part of the binomial.

items.label: Population
items.clue: A group of organisms of the same species living in the same area at the same time, and so able to interbreed.

items.label: Annotation
items.clue: A label on a drawing that gives information about the structure, in particular its function, rather than just its name.

questions.stem: Which description of the structure of a Bacillus cell is correct?

options.text: The DNA is enclosed by a nuclear membrane inside a small nucleus within the cytoplasm.
The cell wall outside the plasma membrane is built from long parallel fibres of cellulose.
A loop of naked DNA lies in the cytoplasm, and proteins are made on 70S ribosomes.
The DNA loop is wound around histone proteins to package it within the nucleoid region.

questions.stem: Which statement correctly describes a membrane-bound organelle of a eukaryotic cell?

options.text: The Golgi apparatus is a stack of flattened sacs studded with ribosomes that synthesize proteins.
Lysosomes are vesicles bounded by a single membrane that contain hydrolytic enzymes.
Mitochondria are bounded by a single membrane folded inward to form cristae.
Secretory vesicles are lysosomes under another name, digesting worn-out organelles.

questions.explanation: Lysosomes are one of the variety of vesicles in eukaryotic cells: single-membrane sacs containing hydrolytic enzymes, kept separate from the rest of the cytoplasm, that digest material taken in and worn-out organelles.

questions.stem: Which row correctly compares the cells of animals, fungi and plants?

options.text: Cell wall: absent in animals, made of cellulose in fungi, made of cellulose in plants.
Vacuoles: absent in animals, present in fungi, present as a large sap vacuole in plants.
Centrioles: present in animals, absent in fungi, present in plants to form the spindle.
Cell wall: absent in animals, made of chitin in fungi, made of cellulose in plants.

questions.stem: Which statement correctly describes the number of nuclei in an atypical eukaryotic cell?

options.text: A mature red blood cell keeps a single nucleus so that it can control the making of haemoglobin.
An aseptate fungal hypha contains many nuclei within one continuous cytoplasm.
A skeletal muscle fibre has a single, very large nucleus to control its whole length.
A phloem sieve tube element is a dead cell, so it has no nucleus and no cytoplasm.

questions.explanation: Aseptate hyphae have no cross-walls, so repeated nuclear division without division of the cytoplasm leaves many nuclei sharing a single continuous cytoplasm inside one plasma membrane.

questions.stem: In an electron micrograph of an animal cell, a structure appears as a discrete stack of curved, flattened membrane sacs with small vesicles budding from its edges and no ribosomes attached. Which structure is it?

options.text: Smooth endoplasmic reticulum, where lipids are made
Mitochondrion, where aerobic cell respiration is carried out
Rough endoplasmic reticulum, where secreted proteins are made
Golgi apparatus, where proteins are modified and packaged

questions.stem: Which statement best describes variation between organisms?

options.text: No two individuals are identical in all their traits, and the patterns of variation are the basis for classifying organisms.
Individuals produced by asexual reproduction share one genome and so are identical in all of their traits.
Organisms are classified by a single distinguishing trait, so variation in the other traits is not used in naming them.
Organisms that look markedly different from one another must be members of two different species.

questions.stem: How did Linnaeus define a species?

options.text: As a group that can breed to produce fertile offspring
As a group of organisms that can mate and have offspring
As a group of organisms that share a set of traits
As organisms that look identical in every trait

questions.explanation: Linnaeus used the original morphological concept: a species is a group of organisms with shared traits, which distinguish them from other groups. This remains the practical basis of identification.

questions.stem: Which statement about the scientific name of the tiger, Panthera tigris, is correct?

options.text: The second word, tigris, is on its own enough to identify the species of tiger.
It should be written Panthera Tigris, because both of its words are proper nouns.
Panthera tigris and Panthera leo are varieties of one species and interbreed freely.
Panthera names the genus and tigris distinguishes the species within it.

questions.explanation: In the binomial system the first part of the name identifies the genus and the second part distinguishes the species from other species in that genus. Panthera leo, the lion, shares the genus and has similar traits.

questions.stem: According to the biological species concept, what is a species?

options.text: A group of organisms that can mate and produce offspring of any kind
A group of organisms that can breed together and produce fertile offspring
A group of organisms that resemble one another in every visible trait
A group of organisms that live in the same area and interbreed with one another

questions.explanation: The biological species concept defines a species as a group of organisms that can breed with one another and produce fertile offspring. Fertility of the offspring is the decisive condition.

questions.stem: Which statement about speciation is correct?

options.text: It is the splitting of one species into two or more, usually happening gradually as populations become more different.
It occurs at the moment when a single mutation produces the first individual of a new species.
It ends at a definite point that can be identified by testing whether the populations are separate.
It is complete as soon as a population becomes geographically separated from the rest of its species.

questions.stem: Which statement about chromosome numbers is correct?

options.text: Humans must have more chromosomes than chimpanzees, because humans are the more complex and advanced organism.
Human diploid cells have 46 chromosomes, chimpanzee diploid cells have 48, and diploid numbers are even.
Human body cells contain 23 chromosomes in total, which is why a diploid number can be an odd number.
Chromosome number determines genome size, so 48 chromosomes must contain more DNA than 46.

questions.stem: Which set of features is used to classify the chromosomes when a karyogram is prepared?

options.text: Length only, so that chromosomes of equal size are matched into pairs
Number of genes and total amount of DNA in each chromosome
Base sequence differences, seen directly as bands on the chromosome
Length, position of the centromere, and banding pattern

questions.explanation: Chromosomes in a karyogram are classified by their length, by the position of the centromere, which sets the relative lengths of the two arms, and by the pattern of bands produced by staining.

questions.stem: Which statement about the genetic material of viruses is correct?

options.text: It is DNA or RNA, and either type may be single-stranded or double-stranded.
It is DNA in every virus, with RNA also present, as in a living cell.
It is RNA in every virus, and is copied into DNA by reverse transcriptase.
It is double-stranded DNA in every virus, as it is in bacteriophage lambda.

questions.explanation: Viral genomes are highly diverse: double-stranded DNA in bacteriophage lambda, single-stranded RNA in coronaviruses and HIV, and single-stranded DNA or double-stranded RNA in other groups. Each virus has one type of nucleic acid.

questions.stem: A single lambda phage infects an E. coli cell in a large culture. Each lytic cycle takes 40 minutes and ends with lysis releasing 100 phages, every one of which immediately infects a fresh cell. How many phages are released by the lysis events that occur 120 minutes after the first infection?
In 2009 a new strain of influenza A appeared with genome segments derived from swine, avian and human influenza viruses, and it caused a pandemic. Which process produced this strain?

options.text: Gradual accumulation of point mutations in the haemagglutinin gene of one strain.
Reverse transcription of the viral RNA followed by insertion of host genes.
Mutation of the virus in response to widespread vaccination against the earlier strains.
Reassortment of RNA genome segments in a cell infected by two different strains.
